newsitem.title: ISRAEL: SOCCER-REVAMPED ISRAEL BEAT CYPRUS 2-0 IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REVAMPED ISRAEL BEAT CYPRUS 2-0 IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Israel, much revamped after disciplinary troubles, kept their lead at the top of European group five after scoring a convincing 2-0 win over Cyprus in their World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
Veteran striker Eli Ohana scored both goals, the first after three minutes and the second with 18 minutes to go.
Israel lead the group on 13 points, two clear of Russia who beat Luxembourg 3-0 in Moscow.

The first Israeli goal came after a bad defensive error between Neophytos Larkou and the goalkeeper, Nicos Panayiotou. The defender failed to make a decisive backpass to his keeper, allowing Ohana in to stroke the ball into an empty net.
The Israelis had many more chances as they dominated the first half, but the second half was more evenly poised.
The Cypriots almost managed to equalise after 71 minutes when a mixup in the Israeli area allowed Yannis Ioanu to shoot at goal, but keeper Rafi Cohen managed to deflect the ball away with his legs.

Israel effectively sealed the result immediately afterwards when a breakaway caught the Cypriots still holding their heads after their miss. A long ball saw a perfect pass to Ohana who slid the ball into the net.
"We were a little unlucky, we played better in the second half but the Israelis were better all round," said Cyprus coach Stavros Papadopoulos.
"They were lucky we didn't score five or six against them," said Israel coach Shlomo Scharf.
Scharf had drastically shuffled his lineup following the dumping of five players due to disciplinary problems the previous day.
"I have to commend my players, they did an excellent job. The most important thing is that they played responsibly and ensured our win," he said.

Israel: 1-Rafi Cohen, 2-Alon Harazi, 3-Moshe Glam, 4-Alon Hazan, 5-Amir Shelah, 6-Arik Bennado, 7-Tal Banin, 8-Alon Mizrahi, (14-Avishai Janno 85), 9-Eyal Berkovic, 10-Itzik Zohar, (15-Reuven Atar 88), 11-Eli Ohana.

Cyprus: 1-Nicos Panayiotou, 2-George Theodotou, 3-Pambos Pittas, 4-Angelos Misos, 5-Marios Charalambous, 6-Neophytos Larkou, (14-Yiannakis Okkas 45) 7-Nicos Timotheou, 8-Sozos Andreou, 9- Sinisa Gogic, 10-Costas Malekos, (Yiannos Ioannou 45), 11-Nick Papavassiliou (12-Yiotis Engomitis 88).
